family.name: EDU7-v1 seven-layer RS-485 exchange
family.claim: Original educational implementation of explicit layer responsibilities; no ISO OSI protocol-suite conformance claim

topology.equipment: Three declared MCU endpoints, router with two independent UARTs, four THVD1400 3.3-V transceiver adapters; two isolated bench segments each no more than 1 m of nominal 120-ohm twisted pair, terminated 120 ohm at both ends
topology.physical_gate: Actual voltage/polarity/wiring, common reference, termination resistance with power off, UART bit timing, DE release after final stop bit, no overlapping drivers, disconnect/reconnect and end-to-end relay captures; host traces close no physical criterion

L1.uart: 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit; no UART error is accepted as clean data
L1.adapter: THVD1400 at 3.3 V; D=UART TX, R=UART RX, RE held low, DE controlled separately. Receiver stays enabled; local echo is explicitly filtered by transmitter ownership.
L1.turnaround: DE asserted 200 us before transmission; retained until UART transmission-complete reports the final stop bit; release then a 200 us guard before a peer may drive. These are lab policies; captured waveforms and actual part timing must validate them.
L1.service: Owned transmit span accepted or BUSY; ordered receive octets plus UART fault events, never a guarantee of error-free delivery

L2.escaping: Within the body, 0x7e and 0x7d become 0x7d followed by byte XOR 0x20; delimiter at both ends. Empty delimiters are ignored; trailing escape or overlong body is dropped through the next delimiter.
L2.crc: CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE: polynomial0x1021, init0xffff, refin=false, refout=false, xorout0; cover all body bytes before CRC; check123456789=>0x29b1
L2.arbitration: Link address1 is the master. Once per25ms turn it sends at most one queued DATA then a zero-payload POLL. Address2 begins one DATA or EMPTY reply within2ms after POLL and guards, then finishes within10ms of its first octet. Slave never transmits without grant. Invalid grant/foreign address/CRC drops produce no upper delivery. Master waits for the completed reply or these bounded deadlines before the next turn; a reply that has begun is not discarded by the start-of-reply deadline.
L2.service: One validated local-link SDU up to40 bytes, or explicit busy/drop/fault result; no link retransmission, upper L4 handles loss

L3.forwarding: Source starts hop_limit=4. Destination consumes with positive hop limit. Router drops hop_limit<=1, unknown route, own-origin loop or bad length/protocol; otherwise decrement hop limit, preserve network src/dst and payload, rebuild link addresses and CRC on the other segment. No broadcast, dynamic routing or L3 fragmentation.
L3.service: Unreliable bounded end-to-end datagram between node IDs; router owns a private copy before releasing input link span

L4.payload: DATA has1..24 octets. All non-final fragments are24 bytes; total SDU1..120 bytes. ACK/PROBE have no payload. Service ports7 and8 are fixed endpoint SAPs; routing never uses port.
L4.state: One outstanding fragment per direction; one reassembly per (src node,src port,dst port). ACK must match tuple, transfer ID and fragment index. Duplicate accepted fragment is re-ACKed without duplicate delivery; unexpected index/count is rejected. Completion publishes a whole SDU atomically then frees reassembly.
L4.flow_and_failure: Credit0 pauses new data; PROBE after100ms asks for current credit without consuming data. Credit1 permits one fragment. Timeout100ms with at most3 retransmissions of the same bytes/index; then fail and clear partial SDU. An independent500ms zero-credit resource deadline reports blocked transfer. Transfer IDs never reused within an active session; wrap forces session reopen.
L4.service: Complete bounded message or explicit failed/blocked result, not a byte-stream socket
L4.completed_receipt: Transfer IDs start1 and strictly increase per direction within session/epoch; no wrap/reuse. Remember highest completed ID and one last completed receipt (tuple,ID,count,last index,last fragment bytes). Repeated matching last fragment is ACKed without publication; older completed IDs are dropped without publication. Replace receipt only on next complete transfer, clear on session reopen. Pending upper consumption retains one complete SDU and advertises credit0 until released.

L5.negotiation: OPEN/OPEN_ACK payload is schema_id:u8=1,unit_id:u8=1,initial_token_node:u8=17. One session A<->B, ports7<->8. Incompatible schema/units or unknown epoch returns ERROR and no application delivery. OPEN and OPEN_ACK use checkpoint0; TOKEN, CLOSE and ERROR also use checkpoint0. DATA uses the next per-direction positive checkpoint; RESUME identifies that direction's last committed checkpoint. All multioctet integers are big-endian.
L5.dialogue: Only token holder sends DATA. TOKEN payload is new_holder_node:u8 and transfers dialogue right after its successful transport delivery. Start with A; A sends request then transfers token to B, B responds then returns token to A. Sending TOKEN enters TOKEN_PENDING: sender may send no new DATA until matching transport completion; lost ACK may temporarily leave no endpoint allowed to start DATA, never both. Receiver recognizes duplicate token delivery without granting a second change. CLOSE/reopen is required before checkpoint wrap.
L5.checkpoint_and_resume: Each direction starts checkpoint1 and increments only after accepted DATA. Same checkpoint+same payload is a duplicate and never reapplies application effect; different payload at same checkpoint is ERROR. Transport reset permits RESUME with same session/epoch and last committed checkpoint; peer retained RAM state must match. Restarted peer with no state refuses resume. Checkpoints and last response remain in RAM only; no durable exactly-once or authenticated-session claim.
L5.service: READY/DATA/TOKEN/RESUME_FAILED/CLOSED events independent of transport transfer IDs

L6.encoding: schema_id:u8=1 followed by ascending unique TLVs: tag:u8,length:u8,value:length. Total presentation PDU<=80 bytes; reject unknown schema, duplicate/out-of-order tags, length mismatch, noncanonical UTF-8 or unrepresentable integer before publication.

tags.4: unit:u8=1 centidegrees Celsius; mandatory for SET and REPLY

L6.service: Typed original application record independent of host struct padding and endianness; optional label is display data, never a C format string
L6.required_fields: All records require verb and request ID. SET requires value and unit1; REPLY requires value and unit1; GET requires neither value nor unit. ERROR may report the retained setpoint with unit1. Known tags have exactly the declared lengths; unknown tags rejected; optional label never changes operation.

L7.application: GET reads the declared fixture plant value; SET changes the declared fixture setpoint only in[-4000,12500] centidegreesC. Request ID matches response, ERROR leaves old setpoint unchanged. Unit1 is mandatory for SET/REPLY. No implication that a physical sensor exists.
L7.acceptance: A routed SET and GET, corrupt frame, wrong route/hop, dropped ACK, duplicate fragment, credit pause, token violation, compatible/incompatible OPEN, retained-state resume and peer reboot refusal, malformed representation and out-of-range SET each have exact state/output oracles
L7.fixture_state: Initial plant value1800 centidegreesC is immutable fixture input. Initial setpoint2200 is mutable. GET returns plant value; successful SET REPLY reports new setpoint. Invalid SET ERROR reports retained setpoint with unit1. Unchanged setpoint is established by explicit state/error-value witness, not by pretending GET reads the setpoint.
